name: Śrī Vaṁśīvadana Ṭhākura
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Kṛṣṇa's flute** (*vaṁśī*) — one of His three famous messengers in Vraja, «the one who accomplishes everything».

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Vaṁśī, the messenger

> vraje vīrā vṛndā vaṁśī ca kṛṣṇasya dūtī-trayam | pragalbha-vacanā vīrā vṛndā ca priya-vādinī, sarva-kārya-sādhikā vaṁśī (Dūtī-bheda, text 4)

«In Vraja, Śrī Kṛṣṇa has three famous messengers: Vīrā, Vṛndā and Vaṁśī. Vīrā is pragalbha-vacanā (a harsh speaker), Vṛndā is priya-vādinī (one who speaks sweetly), and **Vaṁśī, Śrī Kṛṣṇa's flute, is sarva-kārya-sādhikā (one who accomplishes everything)**» (p. 22). Among the pastimes of meeting is «stealing the flute (vaṁśī-caurya)» (p. 51).

## Gopāla-campū — the flute

- **His messenger** (Pūrva-campū 23, verse 40): on the rāsa night, «Inviting them with his flute, his assigned messenger, calling them by means of its friends—streams of perfume, he lured them on a long path with devotion.»
- The brāhmaṇas' wives' «hearts had melted in affection by his attractive rāgas using the skillful, sweet notes of the flute» (Pūrva-campū 22, verse 12). Lalitā: «The mute and deaf flute becomes eloquent under his shelter» (30.60).
- **Who He is** (Uttara-campū 31, verse 46): «Rādhikā is your beloved. Śrīdāma and Subala are your friends. Balarāma is your elder brother. **The flute is your music.**»
- **Left in Vraja** (Uttara-campū 6.48, 32.19): leaving for Mathurā Kṛṣṇa said, «Stoka-kṛṣṇa should wrap himself in my cloth laden with fragrance and play the flute» — He had «entrusted to his representatives the flute, and horn to Stoka-kṛṣṇa and Subala».

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22), p. 51; Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 22.12, 23.40, 30.60; Uttara 6.48, 31.46, 32.19.

name: Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Nārada Muni**, «with a body like Sarasvatī… with an eternal body», the guru of the two reciters of the Gopāla-campū.

## Gopāla-campū — Nārada

- **The guru of Madhukaṇṭha and Snigdhakaṇṭha** (Pūrva-campū 2.89–91): asked where their powers came from, the twin reciters said, «Mercy of guru is the only cause in all cases… It is Nārada, to be remembered every morning, our fortunate possession, who rains all bliss.» Madhumaṅgala too is «equal to Nārada» (2.29) — Paurṇamāsī's boy «seems to be the youthful body of Nārada» (3.71).
- **Meeting Kṛṣṇa after Keśī** (Pūrva-campū 33.30–33): «When he was walking alone, Nārada in bliss met him. Kṛṣṇa saw Nārada approaching dressed in pure clothing.» «He recognized him as Nārada, with a body like Sarasvatī (made of akṣaras or syllables), with an eternal body. Like the Gaṅgā appearing from Viṣṇu's feet, he appeared from the sky… he had an auspicious body with the principal marks of a Vaiṣṇava such as tulasī beads. As a personification of Kṛṣṇa's glories, he filled the ears with various songs… As the full moon holds within itself the dark moon, so he held the form of Kṛṣṇa within his heart.» «Nārada described Kṛṣṇa and Kṛṣṇa described Nārada»; then Nārada told Kṛṣṇa what would come (33.35–55).
- In the Uttara-campū Nārada comes again with news (Uttara-campū 18, 25, 29–30).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 2.29, 2.89–91, 3.71, 33.30–55; Uttara 18, 25, 29–30.

name: Rāmacandra Purī
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Jaṭilā**, Śrī Rādhā's mother-in-law, who entered him (Vibhīṣaṇa of Rāma-līlā is not in these books).

The Gopāla-campū does not name Jaṭilā; it names her son **Abhimanyu**, Rādhā's husband in the eyes of the world — a husband only of an illusion:

- Paurṇamāsī told Vṛndā, «They will not get married to other men. I will prevent this by using my magical powers» — «I have produced for all of them something like a bad dream in a waking state» (Pūrva-campū 15.47–69).
- At Rādhā's wedding with Kṛṣṇa, Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā wept, and «people did not know of the grief caused when they had previously given her to Abhimanyu» (Uttara-campū 35, verse 60). Her parents said to her: «Knowing that Kṛṣṇa was your husband, you spit upon Abhimanyu who mistakenly thought he was your husband» (verse 62).
- «Since Abhimanyu and others had married your replicas, that was acceptable and you married Kṛṣṇa through Paurṇamāsī's arrangements» (Uttara-campū 37, the women bards' praise of Rādhā).
- The Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi: «The prauḍhā beloveds of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, such as Śrīmatī Rādhikā, are certainly parakīyā» — «These girls of Vraja, even though married to young cowherd men, still cherish a strong desire to unite intimately with Śrī Kṛṣṇa… called paroḍhā, or prauḍhā» (Nāyikā-vibhāga, pp. 8–9); Viśvanātha's maidservant-form said Rādhā «is presently at Her in-laws' house at Yāvaṭa» (p. xiv).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.47–69; Uttara 35.60–62, 37; Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, pp. xiv, 8–9.

name: Raghunandana Ṭhākura
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Pradyumna** (Kandarpa), who in Vraja was a **priya-narma-sakhā** of Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Mādhava, helping in Their pastimes.

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the priya-narma-sakhās

«The prema of the priya-narma-sakhās (the most intimate cowherd friends of Kṛṣṇa) in Vraja reaches up to the point of anurāga. The highest point of samarthā-rati in the vraja-gopīs, as well as in Śrī Kṛṣṇa's friends like Subala, extends to the stage of mahābhāva» (Āśraya-nirṇaya, text 15, p. 46). In the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi, Kāmadeva is the example of the *dhīra-lalita* hero, «ever youthful, carefree and controlled by his beloveds' prema» (p. 3).

The Gopāla-campū and the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa do not name this priya-narma-sakhā; here is what they say of Kṛṣṇa's cowherd friends.

## Gopāla-campū — Kṛṣṇa's cowherd friends

- **One life with Him** (Uttara-campū 1, verse 15): «Kṛṣṇa in relation to his friends like Śrīdāma was like the chief life air in relation to the other bodily airs. Always acting as one, they performed all their actions for one purpose—pleasing him.» «Served by his friends, Kṛṣṇa was a likeness of the life air of these boys who had bodies similar to his, for they could not exist without him or without service to him and he had given himself to them» (verse 16).
- «He was the essence of the heart to the cowherds who served him such as Śrīdāma» (Uttara-campū 2, verse 4).
- **Their names** in the Bhāgavatam, quoted in the Gopāla-campū (Pūrva-campū 22.3): «O Stoka-kṛṣṇa and Aṃśu, O Śrīdāma, Subala and Arjuna, O Vṛṣabha, Ojasvī, Devaprastha and Varūthapa!» (SB 10.22.31).
- **The strongest** (Pūrva-campū 14.10): «Śrīdāma, Subala and Stoka-kṛṣṇa, who had strength similar to theirs, assembled with Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. They all understood the hidden meaning of things and followed the principles of dharma. Therefore they were firm friends. It is said they had powers equal to that of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma» — and they asked them for the fruits of the tāla forest guarded by Dhenuka.
- **Their games** (Pūrva-campū 16, verse 14): «Kṛṣṇa played the king, Stoka-kṛṣṇa played the minister, while Balarāma played another king and Subala played his minister. Śrīdāma and Bhadra were the commanders of the army.» «Arjuna, Subala and others began singing using their hands, horns, and split bamboo to keep rhythm. Kṛṣṇa began to dance» (16, verse 7).
- **What Kṛṣṇa is** (Uttara-campū 31, verse 46): «Holder of Govardhana! Your father and mother are Nanda and Yaśodā. Rādhikā is your beloved. **Śrīdāma and Subala are your friends.** Balarāma is your elder brother. The flute is your music.»
- **Their own weddings** (Uttara-campū 35.56): after Kṛṣṇa's wedding with the gopīs, «Śrīdāma and others who had previously remained at kaumāra age by their own will (and therefore did not get married while Kṛṣṇa was gone) then got married.»

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the love of His friends

> vrajastha-priya-narma-sakhānāṁ ca anurāga-paryantā | vraja-sundarīṇaṁ tu samarthā ratiḥ mahābhāva-paryantā, subalādīnāṁ ca (Āśraya-nirṇaya, text 15)

«The prema of the priya-narma-sakhās (the most intimate cowherd friends of Kṛṣṇa) in Vraja reaches up to the point of anurāga. The highest point of samarthā-rati in the vraja-gopīs, as well as in Śrī Kṛṣṇa's friends like Subala, extends to the stage of mahābhāva» (p. 46).

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, p. 3; Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 14.10, 16.7, 16.14, 22.3; Uttara 1.15–16, 2.4, 31.46, 35.56; Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Āśraya-nirṇaya 15 (pp. 45–46).

name: Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

By Kṛṣṇa's mercy **Sadāśiva** took the form of a **cowherd boy** and danced with Kṛṣṇa in Vraja (the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā).

name: Acyutānanda (son of Advaita)
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

The gopī **Acyutā**, present in him (with Kārttikeya, who is not in Vraja).

The Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa and the Gopāla-campū do not name Acyutā. What the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi says of the sakhīs who love Śrī Rādhā more and of Her maidservants:

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the sakhīs who love Śrī Rādhā more

> atha sakhī pañca-vidhā | sakhī, nitya-sakhī, prāṇa-sakhī, priya-sakhī, parama-preṣṭhā-sakhī | āsāṁ madhye kācit sama-snehā kācid asama-snehā | … yā rādhikāyāṁ snehādhikā sā nitya-sakhī |
> nitya-sakhyas tu kastūrī manojñā maṇi-mañjarī
> sindūrā candanavatī kaumudī madirādayaḥ (Sakhī-bheda, text 5)

- «There are five different types of sakhīs: (1) sakhī, (2) nitya-sakhī, (3) prāṇa-sakhī, (4) priya-sakhī and (5) parama-preṣṭha-sakhī. Of these, some possess equal affection for both Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa (sama-sneha), while others are partial to either Śrī Rādhā or Śrī Kṛṣṇa (viṣama-sneha).»
- «**Those sakhīs with more affection for Śrīmatī Rādhikā are called nitya-sakhīs.** They include Kasturī, Manojñā, Maṇi Mañjarī, Sindūrā, Candanavatī, Kaumudī and Madirā.»
- «The most prominent nitya-sakhīs are known as prāṇa-sakhīs. Examples are Tulasī, Keli-kandalī, Kādambarī, Śaśimukhī, Candralekhā, Priyambadā, Madonmadā, Madhumatī, Vasantī, Kalabhāṣinī, Ratnāvalī, Mālatī and Karpūralatikā. All of these gopīs are equal in beauty to Vṛndāvaneśvarī Śrīmatī Rādhikā.»
- «Vraja damsels such as Mālatī, Candralatikā, Guṇachūḍā, Varāṅgadā, Mādhavī, Candrikā, Prema Mañjarī, Tanumadhyamā and Kandarpa-sundarī are ten million in number. They are all examples of priya-sakhīs» (pp. 23–25).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the maidservants

- **Paricārikās**: among the messengers who bring Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa together, «Sakhīs such as **Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Bhānumatī Mañjarī** are called paricārikā, servants, or assistants… According to the necessity of the time, all sakhīs act as messengers» (Dūtī-bheda, text 4, p. 22). «A nisṛṣṭārthā-dūtī performs all services upon receiving a command and personally shoulders the total responsibility of arranging the meeting between Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa» (p. 21).
- **A maidservant of Rādhā** (introduction, pp. xiii–xiv): when envious scholars waited in a grove to kill Viśvanātha Cakravartī, «he suddenly disappeared, and in his place, a beautiful young girl of Vraja appeared, picking flowers with her friends… she replied, “I am a maidservant of my mistress, Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She is presently at Her in-laws' house at Yāvaṭa. She has sent me here to pick flowers.”»
- **Their mistress**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā is His constitutional pleasure potency (svarūpa-bhūtā-hlādinī-śakti)… The other gopīs are Śrīmatī Rādhikā's direct and non-different expansions (kāya-vyūha), manifestations (prakāśa) or partial manifestations (aṁśa-svarūpa)» (pp. 3–4). «Although mohana-mahābhāva is awakened within all the sakhīs in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's yūtha (group), it is most awakened in Śrīmatī Rādhikā» (p. 43).
- **Her group's love**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā and the gopīs who follow Her possess mañjiṣṭhā-rāga, which is independent, having no basis other than itself. It eternally increases and becomes more and more splendid» (p. 41); «Adhirūḍha-mahābhāva is seen only in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's group» (p. 46).

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, pp. xiii–xiv, 3–4, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22), Sakhī-bheda 5 (pp. 23–25), Rati-bheda (pp. 41–43), Āśraya-nirṇaya 15 (p. 46).

name: Kāśīnātha Paṇḍita (of Navadvīpa)
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Kulaka**, the brāhmaṇa whom King Satrājit sent to Kṛṣṇa to arrange His marriage with Satyabhāmā. The Gopāla-campū does not name him; it tells how Satrājit gave Satyabhāmā to Kṛṣṇa:

## Gopāla-campū — Satrājit (Uttara-campū 17)

- «Satrājit, who performed sacrifices to please the sun, having pleased the sun» received the jewel (17.13); proud, he «does not offer the jewel to Kṛṣṇa» (17.16).
- When the jewel was found, Kṛṣṇa «called Satrājit to the assembly with respect. After relating all that had happened, he finally gave the jewel to him with a smile» (17.59). «First the jewel turned away from Kṛṣṇa and then turned face downwards (in shame) to Satrājit» (verse 7).
- «Satrājit began to think, “Kṛṣṇa is secretly angry with me. How can I satisfy him?… By giving my jewel of a daughter, even more valuable, along with this jewel, I will satisfy him.”» «He gave his daughter named Satyabhāmā along with the jewel… Satyabhāmā's bhakti was unlimited… His lack of devotion has been described» (17.62–64).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 17.13–64 (verses 7–8).

name: Kāśīśvara Brahmacārī (disciple of Īśvara Purī)
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Bhṛṅgāra**, one of Kṛṣṇa's servants (*ceṭas*) in Vṛndāvana — with Govinda, who was Bhaṅgura; and **Śaśirekhā**, a gopī of Vraja.

The Gopāla-campū and the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa do not name Bhṛṅgāra. What the Gopāla-campū says of the servants of Kṛṣṇa's house:

## Gopāla-campū — Kṛṣṇa's servants, singers and dancers

- **In His going out** (Pūrva-campū 2.64): «When Kṛṣṇa departed with Śrīrāma, Dāma and others, servants followed him with umbrella, cāmara, cloves and a box of betel, rare even for devatās.»
- **His care for them** (Uttara-campū 6.49–51): leaving Vraja, «Seeing his servants—the śūdras, abhīras, and young boys without discriminating power—and Nanda standing silently, Kṛṣṇa with tears in his eyes said, “Since they are all affectionate like my friends or my father and the elders, they will attain service following the elders and be praiseworthy.”» «Honoring his servants suitably, he informed the elders of their services.»
- **His wedding procession** (Uttara-campū 35.3): «Experts in heavenly music played the music. The dancers were skillful in dancing and singing. Priests walked in front… His friends walked on either side. **Servants walked while holding cāmaras.**»
- **His nurses**: «I remember Kṛṣṇa, the good fortune of Vraja, repeating new words like a parrot, pointing to objects and asking about them with his finger, being taught words by his nurses» (Pūrva-campū 6, verse 67); after lunch «the nurse gave him a golden box» of betel (10.23).
- **The singers of His pastimes**: the whole Gopāla-campū is sung in Nanda's assembly by the twin reciters Madhukaṇṭha and Snigdhakaṇṭha, disciples of Nārada (Pūrva-campū 2.69–91, 3.12).


## Śaśirekhā

The Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa and the Gopāla-campū do not name Śaśirekhā. What the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi says of the sakhīs who love Śrī Rādhā more and of Her maidservants:

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the sakhīs who love Śrī Rādhā more

> atha sakhī pañca-vidhā | sakhī, nitya-sakhī, prāṇa-sakhī, priya-sakhī, parama-preṣṭhā-sakhī | āsāṁ madhye kācit sama-snehā kācid asama-snehā | … yā rādhikāyāṁ snehādhikā sā nitya-sakhī |
> nitya-sakhyas tu kastūrī manojñā maṇi-mañjarī
> sindūrā candanavatī kaumudī madirādayaḥ (Sakhī-bheda, text 5)

- «There are five different types of sakhīs: (1) sakhī, (2) nitya-sakhī, (3) prāṇa-sakhī, (4) priya-sakhī and (5) parama-preṣṭha-sakhī. Of these, some possess equal affection for both Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa (sama-sneha), while others are partial to either Śrī Rādhā or Śrī Kṛṣṇa (viṣama-sneha).»
- «**Those sakhīs with more affection for Śrīmatī Rādhikā are called nitya-sakhīs.** They include Kasturī, Manojñā, Maṇi Mañjarī, Sindūrā, Candanavatī, Kaumudī and Madirā.»
- «The most prominent nitya-sakhīs are known as prāṇa-sakhīs. Examples are Tulasī, Keli-kandalī, Kādambarī, Śaśimukhī, Candralekhā, Priyambadā, Madonmadā, Madhumatī, Vasantī, Kalabhāṣinī, Ratnāvalī, Mālatī and Karpūralatikā. All of these gopīs are equal in beauty to Vṛndāvaneśvarī Śrīmatī Rādhikā.»
- «Vraja damsels such as Mālatī, Candralatikā, Guṇachūḍā, Varāṅgadā, Mādhavī, Candrikā, Prema Mañjarī, Tanumadhyamā and Kandarpa-sundarī are ten million in number. They are all examples of priya-sakhīs» (pp. 23–25).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the maidservants

- **Paricārikās**: among the messengers who bring Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa together, «Sakhīs such as **Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Bhānumatī Mañjarī** are called paricārikā, servants, or assistants… According to the necessity of the time, all sakhīs act as messengers» (Dūtī-bheda, text 4, p. 22). «A nisṛṣṭārthā-dūtī performs all services upon receiving a command and personally shoulders the total responsibility of arranging the meeting between Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa» (p. 21).
- **A maidservant of Rādhā** (introduction, pp. xiii–xiv): when envious scholars waited in a grove to kill Viśvanātha Cakravartī, «he suddenly disappeared, and in his place, a beautiful young girl of Vraja appeared, picking flowers with her friends… she replied, “I am a maidservant of my mistress, Śrīmatī Rādhikā. She is presently at Her in-laws' house at Yāvaṭa. She has sent me here to pick flowers.”»
- **Their mistress**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā is His constitutional pleasure potency (svarūpa-bhūtā-hlādinī-śakti)… The other gopīs are Śrīmatī Rādhikā's direct and non-different expansions (kāya-vyūha), manifestations (prakāśa) or partial manifestations (aṁśa-svarūpa)» (pp. 3–4). «Although mohana-mahābhāva is awakened within all the sakhīs in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's yūtha (group), it is most awakened in Śrīmatī Rādhikā» (p. 43).
- **Her group's love**: «Śrīmatī Rādhikā and the gopīs who follow Her possess mañjiṣṭhā-rāga, which is independent, having no basis other than itself. It eternally increases and becomes more and more splendid» (p. 41); «Adhirūḍha-mahābhāva is seen only in Śrīmatī Rādhikā's group» (p. 46).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 2.64, 2.69–91, 3.12, 6.67, 10.23; Uttara 6.49–51, 35.3; Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, pp. xiii–xiv, 3–4, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22), Sakhī-bheda 5 (pp. 23–25), Rati-bheda (pp. 41–43), Āśraya-nirṇaya 15 (p. 46).

name: Garuḍa Paṇḍita
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa's pastimes

**Garuḍa**, the eagle who carries the Lord.

## Gopāla-campū — Garuḍa

- In the fight for the pārijāta, Kṛṣṇa, «Mounting Garuḍa with Satyabhāmā… carrying Nandaka, the best of swords, went to Prāgjyotiṣa» (Uttara-campū 18.25); «Seeing that fort while on Garuḍa, Kṛṣṇa was amazed and he made Satyabhāmā's hairs stand on end for fun» (verse 12); «Keeping Satyabhāmā on the back of Garuḍa, Kṛṣṇa landed on earth» (18.52).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Uttara 18.25–52 (verse 12).
